import pandas as pd
from typing import Optional

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract the watermark high_ts value
    high_ts = watermark.loc[0, "high_ts"]
    
    # Filter events: keep only those with event_ts > high_ts
    filtered_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # If no events to process, return the target snapshot as-is
    if filtered_events.empty:
        return {"new_snapshot": target_snapshot}
    
    # Sort events by (event_ts, event_seq) to identify the latest event per product_id
    # event_seq acts as a tie-breaker for deterministic ordering
    filtered_events = filtered_events.sort_values(
        by=["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
        ascending=[True, True, True]
    )
    
    # Keep only the latest event per product_id (last row after sorting)
    latest_events = filtered_events.drop_duplicates(
        subset=["product_id"],
        keep="last"
    )
    
    # Separate deletes and upserts
    delete_events = latest_events[latest_events["op"] == "D"]
    upsert_events = latest_events[latest_events["op"].isin(["I", "U"])]
    
    # Remove deleted products from the snapshot
    if not delete_events.empty:
        deleted_product_ids = set(delete_events["product_id"])
        target_snapshot = target_snapshot[~target_snapshot["product_id"].isin(deleted_product_ids)]
    
    # Upsert records (update or insert)
    if not upsert_events.empty:
        for _, event in upsert_events.iterrows():
            product_id = event["product_id"]
            name = event["name"]
            price = event["price"]
            event_ts = event["event_ts"]
            
            # Check if product exists in snapshot
            mask = target_snapshot["product_id"] == product_id
            if mask.any():
                # Update existing record
                target_snapshot.loc[mask, "name"] = name
                target_snapshot.loc[mask, "price"] = price
                target_snapshot.loc[mask, "last_event_ts"] = event_ts
            else:
                # Insert new record
                new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                    "product_id": [product_id],
                    "name": [name],
                    "price": [price],
                    "last_event_ts": [event_ts]
                })
                target_snapshot = pd.concat(
                    [target_snapshot, new_row],
                    ignore_index=True
                )
    
    # Ensure correct dtypes
    target_snapshot = target_snapshot.astype({
        "product_id": "int64",
        "name": "object",
        "price": "float64",
        "last_event_ts": "datetime64[us]"
    })
    
    return {"new_snapshot": target_snapshot}
